tips.comment: Pedley Wood completed the double before being pulled up last time out. If back to that sort of form, then could go close here and money back for each way, which shouldn't be a problem.

Peejaybee returned at the back of the pack last month, but that was in a C2. Last year, he did win off a 114 and was a close second in a C4 at Market Rasen in January off today's mark. He is worth another shot now back in C4 again.

Drops back in trip slightly following a solid run behind a thriving horse last time out. As mentioned above, he ran a cracker last time out behind a thriving horse in Yes Day. Beaten 7L by the winner albeit. That form got boosted with the winner going in again next time out off a 5lbs higher mark. He had 1 run at this venue in his novice hurdle days, running an absolute cracker behind a high-class horse in The Jukebox Man. Beaten just over 3L by the winner. That type of form is better than anything else in this lineup. This is just his 3rd chase run. He won 1 of his P2P runs over this distance. So if anything, dropping back in trip will suit him. I think he will go well off this weight, with the jockey taking off a further 5lbs also.

After falling on penultimate start Balkardy was re-educated last time in a class 3 over CD. More is sure to be asked of the 8yo today dropped back to class 4 and down another 1lb. Course trip and ground all positives. Has finished first three in 8/12 chase starts and offers EW value at 16/1.
Has excellent course form around here, reads... 2/1/2. Goes on the ground and tries new headgear combo today, having disappointed LTO. Prior to that run, had been shaping up well.

Glengolly ran well in November after a long break and then was unlucky to unseat rider (UR) when going well four out over 3m, good to soft, at Wetherby in December. Pulled up (PU) in January after an early mistake, then came back from a two-month break to finish 5th last time, shaping as if he would come on for the run. Sheehan rides and has a good strike rate for the yard. Last time he rode, it was before he joined this yard. It was a moderate affair, and he has shown he has enough to do well here.
Jukebox Joker looks ready to win a race of this calibre and is well fancied here. Will definitely suit the distance and ground.
Tuscan Rose made her career best succeeding over 3m at Taunton a year ago. She has been twice runner-up from 4 rides since and should get involved again today if suited by circumstances.
Fell last time out but looked very enticing. The trainer is currently in form, and today might be the day.

Not often seen in a class 5 these days, and his record in this class reads 2111pu4. He is currently running 11 lb below its highest winning mark and has the booking of probably the most sought-after 5 lb claimer in S. Fenelon. The trainer's horses are running well at the moment, so I'm in at 12/1.

Indeevar Bleu won a Wetherby bumper in March last year on rules debut and then won at Leicester on his second start over hurdles in December. He was 3rd in a Class 3 novice at Haydock in December. He subsequently had a wind operation, and making his handicap debut in Class 4, looks the most likely winner.
Will be suited to this course, looks an eye catching unexposed type that should be capable of far better than its bare form and looks a big price.

Race 5 at Ffos Las today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 3,184 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 10-year-old gelding Stream of Stars from the Nigel A Twiston-Davies yard and will be ridden by James Turner. This son of Sea The Stars is still competitive and should have a say in the finish. Has to be included.

9yo gelding who has posted 4 top 3 finishes, including 2 victories from 10 starts over hurdles. He has struggled for some time now, but has dropped significantly in the weights and could be dangerous off his current OR of 112, in a race over his preferred distance of 2 miles, where he may be allowed an uncontested lead.
Necronaut looked decent enough on debut, chasing home a decent winner. With 7 pounds in hand here against the market leader, they can go close here.

Peter's Last Deal is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Tom Symonds and owned by Lady Gibbons. He traveled well for a long way on debut and attracted some market support, which suggests more was expected. Now, with a run under his belt, we will probably see some improvement for an owner who has tasted success with Issam winning four times for Tom Symonds. Their Peter's Last Deal can go well under Caoilin Quinn off just 10st 9lb.

Runner-up in Ireland in his only point and filled the same position on stable debut, in an Aintree bumper on Boxing Day. May not have been suited by the heavy ground when only 4th at Exeter last time and looks to have been found a good opportunity.
The Paul Nicholls yard has won a quarter of all NHF races entered in the last 5 seasons. They send 2 runners here to run in each NHF race, and this newcomer could complete an NHF double for the yard.

Makes stable debut today, but did put up a more than decent debut for previous yard, when coming 3/8 beaten 4.5 lengths in a class 5 NHF race over extended 2 miles @ Exeter. Good jockey up who does well for this stable and very good trainer is 1/3 in this sphere here last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Name Me Nicely ran a solid 3rd in an Irish Point-to-Point, which is working out well. This trainer combination is doing well. Kim Bailey (now recently joined with Mat Nicholls) has a good record with bumper horses first time out. This horse has a stout staying pedigree, so the galloping track and softer ground today should help him outrun his odds.

Passage Du Mare is looking hugely underestimated here based on his good connections. Sire: 4-time winner Rail Link, dam: dual winner Tourtour, and EW option looks really impressive at these odds offered!

3-year-old gelding sired by Land Force won his maiden on good to firm back on September 24 and ran a few other races on decent ground. Had a run on heavy after his win and then was given a break and gelded in February. Carrying top weight here and can hopefully give a good show first time back after the operation. Ran well first time out as a maiden and Ryan Moore is booked, so should be given plenty of help from the saddle.
Power Fizz is likely to get back-to-back victories today on its handicap debut, having won at Newcastle in January. Panama Black and Prosperitas seem the candidates to make the frame behind the pick.
Has done well on the AW and has a pedigree for turf. Showed promise and should improve, but is stepping into deeper waters today and might need to find a bit more against stronger types.

Panama Black has been nibbled at in the market to this price, with which we see Billy Loughnane and Brian Meehan teaming up once more. Panama Black looks to be progressing along the right lines and he could be sounding out a very good run here, that can bring him in line with his ability on the all weather this season, indicating he can adapt to both all weather and grass.
Small trainer at the moment, who has learned his trade from Godolphin/Varian, is T Kent, whose stable has popped in a few recently on the AW. Prosperitas is the one he sends to HQ. Interesting.

Did not have the best run LTO when 6 of 8 at Nottingham last October, but tricky conditions to be fair. So expecting a better effort on good going. However, improvements are required as going up in class and challenging starting mark on handicap debut.
A recent gelding that finished 3rd in a Class 2 for his debut race but didn't improve for the two races since. Bred to come good ongoing, so it may be the time to punt.

White Crown Star held on by only a shorthead when claiming his first win from a rapid finishing Fearnot at Kempton over 7f with pacesetter Noble Guest fading into 5th. Could provide another winner for Andrew Balding by following up over 7f off a mark of 78.

He won 2 races as a two-year-old on straight tracks and performed well enough in a 50k race at York and on the AW before being gelded. The effect of that procedure is the determining factor here as there is little else to get interested in within the field.

Valsharah ran some promising races last year which included a 4th of 14 in a 7f handicap at Newbury and started this season with a 3rd last month at Kempton over 7f and could be competitive off bottom weight here.
Love Is The Law is a lightly raced filly with 2 wins from 3 on similar ground, a 7f win already under her belt, and looks primed to progress further if ready after a break.
A winner when last at this venue, but has been abroad, then raced on the all-weather for the past 3 runs at different venues. A return to Newmarket looks like a good idea.
Has the highest mark in this field but is in shocking form since the last win at Southwell last December. Perhaps the starting handicap is just too high, so a dropped mark tomorrow should be welcome.
Drops down in class on handicap debut after struggling in a Class 1 race. Difficult to gauge, but has won at this level, and that could be something to gamble on.

Promise in all 4 of their 2yo runs and makes handicap debut here on 3yo return of decent mark of 76. Step up to this 7f should suit, under used jockey up and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 16/1 worth Ew consideration here.
Goes up 7lb in hat trick bid after following up in January. Has shown improvement since upped in trip and now reverts back to turf. Optimistic that he is just as able on grass.

Race 5 at Ripon is a Handicap (Class 5) for 3-year-olds over 1,609 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Last Shamardal from the Jack Channon yard, and will be ridden by George Bass. This son of Shamardal has improved with each start and is bidding for his hat-trick from just 4 starts to date. Must be considered here.
Flagon Dry is a very interesting horse here, with the last race throwing out winners aplenty at this level. Purely based on this and the ability to dictate the running. Great chance.
Finished well at Wolverhampton last month to get fourth place from an impossible position and will be fitter for that run. Now 1 lb lower as well.

Criminal Surge makes handicap debut and although needs to improve on what he's shown so far, he is bred to be far better than what he has achieved in three novice runs. Related to a number of winners, including a couple of high class performers, who have wins at Group 3 level in Ireland and Grade 3 level in the States.
First run since being gelded and experienced for a three-year-old. Good places at lower level, but first-time cheekpieces may just add something positive.

That Lucas Fella made his career best when 4th of 10 over 6f at Carlisle in August last year. Although unsuccessful in his next 3 rides since, he remains a good value for money option on EW terms here for me.

On The River is a course and distance winner who has been off the track for 167 days and looks to have the best form in this Apprentice Handicap. He has won 10 races and placed 7 times from 43 runs and that should be good enough to win this.
Charlie Johnston can ready one, and this has a good record fresh and a decent jockey in this race to aid. 5 lb below last mark and can outclass if ready to go.

Ridden by Elle-May Croot, who has been successful in this race before and takes the reins on Bowood, who recorded a much-improved victory here last summer. He hasn't shone on the AW, so hoping the return to Ripon brings about the same improvement. Obviously, Dutch Decoy is the danger.
Garden Oasis returns after a third before his break. He looks well-treated, and this could be a good race for him to win when fresh.
It was obvious from the latest run that this one is better over 7 or today's trip, the mile. Should see a much better performance this afternoon and looks to be at a very generous each-way price.
Pisanello is a 5-time winner with distance and class success. Capable fresh, and latest runs have been below par, but conditions suit and past form suggests potential.

Dan Skelton could be finishing the day at Cheltenham on a high with his mare Sheezer Dancer making a mark in this National Hunt flat race. Connections are coming for this race, with her showing up well at home.
Freddiemissmolli shaped nicely on debut and should come on nicely for the run. Can follow it up here under Harry Cobden with another big run and look to pick up some place money.
Definite signs of promise in both their NHF races to date and very good jockey/trainer combination makes current 11/1 the EW play here.

POETISA is a well-bred, unraced four-year-old filly by Poet's Word. She is a half-sister to Queenohearts, a winner of three hurdle races and two NH flat races. The course, distance, and going should suit her. She should run well on her racecourse debut and could well be able to win this race.

In what looks like a very open bumper it could be worth throwing a dart at the superbly bred Rainbow Tara. She is by Kayf Tara, out of a Definite Article mare who is related to some high class sorts, such as Real Steel and there is plenty of Old Vic in the pedigree so there is plenty of stamina. She is also a half sister to Merely A Detail who bolted up in her bumper debut for this trainer at 28/1.

Highly promising Kingman colt who made a sparkling debut at Kempton 135 days ago to finish 1st/13 quickening clear in impressive fashion once asked the question and showed and extremely good turn of foot in the process and strongly appeals as the type to move onto better things now as a 3yo and this looks like an excellent stepping stone for this return to action arriving here in top nick and in very good heart jockey Kieren Shoemark takes the ride on John & Thady Gosden's inmate and can give Bowmark the perfect ride here at Newcastle must be taken seriously representing top connections here . Respected .

Irish raider. The 3yo colt was a nice 3L winner on his debut six weeks ago, posting a high RPR rating. A useful-looking A O’Brien runner was in third that day. The runner-up has run well in a Group 3 since. Some unexposed rivals in this Listed contest, and the selection looks the value bet.

Up 6 lbs for Trial Day win when overcoming a wide trip to win fairly comfortably. Trainer wasn't sure he'd like Lingfield, but he'd won here at Newcastle the time before, so today's track is not a worry. Only 3 years old, plenty of improvement is possible to come. May defy the rise bearing in mind the Trials win wouldn't have suited. Sired by Too Darn Hot from a Lope De Vega mare, he's bred to progress.

The 7/1 looks an e/w steal to me for this progressive horse, which already has some cracking form in the book. This colt showed a great attitude to only go down by a head last time out to a horse that's since performed well in a Group 3 race. Prior to that, Hello Zaman had won well at this trip in another AW race when he had the race sewn up and was eased down. It's that 2nd last time out, though, which is the key for me, and the trainer has his string in great order, so the 7/1 looks very generous, I'd suggest.

Simply can't have that. He's an 11/1 shot here. Won at this level already when beating Rebels Gamble by 1.75L, who since went on to win a Listed race by 1.75L from Rajeko, which stacks up well. Disappointing the next time in Class 4 Southwell Handicap when beaten 0.5L at 5/6. Just seemed to not pick up when needed and was nothing like his previous performance. Maybe uncomfortable under heavy weight; however, he's been dropped 1lb as a result and can go well here.

Very impressive win off 100 LTO when unable to get a run, then putting the race to bed in a matter of strides. Raised 3 lbs for that, and it's not clear if she beat much. However, she'd won a French Listed race the time prior, so chances are it wasn't a one-off. Wind surgery since and possibly more to come, but a repeat of that would likely be all it takes.
The form figures of Quandary this year read well (2321), the win at Lingfield in February reading well giving the selection great chances of finishing in the top 4.

The 4yo filly has 4 wins from 8 and twice a runner-up, looking progressive. Front runner who has a high cruising speed. Two wins and a narrow defeat in her three starts this year, and only slightly higher in the weights now. Unexposed over this 7f trip and she has a strong jockey booking. The fav in the race looks smart but he does like to be held up and with 14 runners he could meet some trouble.
With 4 places available, Storm Star should at least grab a podium finish having won twice here at Newcastle this year with this race targeted since that last win.

Fairly consistent over 6f around this - Listed level. 2 Class 2 and Listed win to start the season before dropping to 5f to finish 0.5L 2nd to Clarendon House. Not the world's best form that run, however, it was encouraging over a suboptimal trip. Followed that up 2.25L 3rd behind Spycatcher on officially Good To Soft. However, with the winner being a Soft ground performer, I think it's safe to assume the ground was on the softer side. Regardless, he never looked overly comfortable throughout, so he has excuses. Would imagine this has been the plan for some time and has every chance to get it done if running to his best.
Diligent Harry is a previous winner of this race and proved his well-being when running 3rd at Southwell just 12 days ago. Conditions look ideal for a big run.

Not too many miles on the clock for the 6yo. Two runs this year, not beaten far three weeks ago in a decent contest and could be ready to strike. He does tend to keep his form once fit and in good shape. He was a close 3rd over this 6f C/D last summer in a Group 3 - didn’t have a clear run, and was beaten by two runners rated 114+. His mark of 105 for this handicap gives him every chance.
Old Harrovian is the win selection after winning very easily when last raced here in January. With Oisin Murphy in the saddle, all looks good for a big run.

Ran a good race to beat Old Harrovian over 1m3f, then followed it up with an impressive win of 3.25L in a class 2 handicap off 2nd top weight. Took a second to get going there, but once in top gear, he put it to bed very quickly. Slight concern the drop to 1m2f might not be optimal. However, he is very lightly raced for a 6yo and could still progress to a graded performer.

Lightly raced 4yo. Coming good this year with back-to-back wins. Impressive last time out, coming from off the pace, the jockey was still pretty much motionless as he passed through the line when winning by 2L+. He’s had a nice 11 weeks off the track, maybe to keep his current mark, and no reason why he can’t progress again.
For a horse with all-weather form figures of 11112 since September, current double-figure odds look generous, especially with the apprentice jockey claiming 5 lb.

Top weight is always a concern, but the manner in which he won last time out when pulling clear by 5 lengths in the trial was very impressive. Up 8 lbs as a result; however, I'm pretty sure he had more than 8 lbs in hand with that win. Course and distance winner. Connections talked about the Dubai Gold Cup, and they're pretty confident that he's a Cup horse. Should be 6/4 in my opinion.

Wonder Legend has a very consistent record on the all weather (23121 since September) and last month's win at Wolverhampton was so impressive that it is hard to see the next best bet of the day not being involved in the finish.

Lightly raced 4yo, five runs on the AW and hasn’t been out of the first two places - improved RPR rating with each run. A good second last time out, seeing the race out well but not quite getting to the winner - who got the first run and wasn’t stopping. He meets that winner again but on 4lb better terms now, this extra 2f can suit him and he has Oisin Murphy taking over in the saddle.

Promising seven pound claimer up which brings the weight down to a very handy spot after a good last start win in which he carried the same as the handicap weight allocated for this event. That augurs well for chances here when you consider master trainer James Owen has gone with the apprentice option to enhance Destinado's chances.

A very open middle-distance handicap where Raintown looks great value at 14/1. He won well here a couple of runs back and should be competitive from 3 pounds higher. He likes to race on the front end and may get the run of the race.

Good odds for a horse that probably, on paper, is the best here. After a recent break and wind operation with a 7lb claimer on board who won on penultimate start, I think it can go well for a yard in form. Has form ahead of Kings Code, which is solid benchmark form and could be a better model now.
Party Bear is improving in leaps and bounds and has the ability to take this and run up a hat-trick of wins. Karl Burke's yard has him primed.

Richard Kingscote to ride, and that should be a big assist. Trainer and rider have all-weather strike rates above 10%. This is a very consistent horse, rarely out of the money, and with a course record of a win and a placing from two starts here and a 100% record on the polytrack surface, looks well placed.

Dual-purpose type who flits between hurdling and staying flat races. Is a previous CD winner here in December 2024 in class 5, winning off a mark of 70. Is running off 71 today, the same mark as when running here 17 days ago, finishing 3rd, narrowly beaten by one of today's rivals, Dance Time, but who is now better off at weights. Although that race was over 13f, today's step up to 16f should suit more.

Charlatan was hampered last time out, and that ninth placing would best be forgiven when assessing chances of this, I feel. 16-3-7 record in this ground. Placed on the course. Callum Shepherd clicks with the horse well, as his 9-4-2 record attests. That third at Wolverhampton at penultimate run was solid. Has ability as demonstrated by winning three in a row last term and then winning first-up in current preparation. It all adds up to a better effort this time of asking.

The 3yo has 1 win from 5. He was 3rd in a good quality AW handicap two weeks ago, after coming off a 7 month break, something to build on and the benefit of that recent run will be a positive factor. His novice stakes win on his third start last year is decent looking form. He looks overpriced.

The 4yo was progressive last year, winning his final three starts during the autumn. No problem with the winter break and was a good 3rd last week over this 7f C/D, in a good quality handicap - always having a bit too much to do after a slow start but stayed on well. Same mark for this contest and he should be better for that last run.

The 4yo was quite busy last year, 3 wins and useful on his day. No ill effect earlier in the month after returning from a 6 month break, 3rd of 10 in a good quality handicap, only outpaced in the last 100 yards. Something to build on and is on a handy looking mark.

Not too many miles on the clock for the 4yo. Progressive last year, winning three in a row last summer, including a useful £52K handicap over this 14f trip - only 3lb higher now. A big run earlier in the month after coming off his winter break, beaten under a length in a good quality Listed race. Back in handicap company for this contest and every chance he can continue the improvement this year.

The 5yo has been below par this winter but got his act together five weeks ago, never in trouble when winning a four runner contest by 7L. His stats suggest he should be better on this quicker ground - he won a decent £16K handicap last autumn on quick ground. Still on a decent mark and his six rivals don’t look great.

Just four hurdle runs for the unexposed 6yo, form 2313. He ran a good race on his handicap debut five weeks ago - over this 3m trip - he was in second and poised to challenge 2 out but made a mess of the hurdle, losing his momentum, not given a hard time after and stayed on nicely to finish third. Something to build on. Same mark for this handicap, strong jockey booking and too early to write off.

The 11yo took well to fences in the last 12 months, winning three times. His last race was maybe one run too many. Two starts back he was beaten just 2L by the smart ‘Numitor’, who has boosted that form since and the selection now meets that rival on 10lb better terms in this race. He loves the quicker ground and has been kept under wraps for the last 5 months with this nice £51K veterans’ chase prize being the target.
